name: Bloaters
description: Code, methods and classes that have grown so large they are hard to work with.

smells.name: Long Method
smells.summary: A function does too many things and spans too many lines; the longer it is, the harder it is to understand, test and reuse.

smells.name: Large Class / God Class
smells.summary: A class with too many fields, methods and responsibilities that knows and does everything.

smells.name: Long Parameter List
smells.summary: Functions with more than three or four parameters, hard to call correctly and to read.

smells.name: Primitive Obsession
smells.summary: Using primitive types (string, int) for domain concepts such as money, emails or ranges instead of dedicated types.

smells.name: Data Clumps
smells.summary: The same groups of variables travel together everywhere (street, city, zip) without being grouped into an object.

name: Object-Orientation Abusers
description: Incomplete or incorrect application of object-oriented programming principles.

smells.name: Switch Statements / Repeated Switches
smells.summary: The same switch or if/else chain on a type is repeated in several places; every new type forces you to touch them all.

smells.name: Temporary Field
smells.summary: Fields that only hold a value under certain circumstances and are empty the rest of the time.

smells.name: Refused Bequest
smells.summary: A subclass inherits methods and data it does not want or cannot use, violating the Liskov Substitution Principle.

smells.name: Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces
smells.summary: Two classes do the same thing with different names and signatures, so they cannot be swapped.

smells.name: Base Class Depending on Its Derivatives
smells.summary: A base class knows about or references its subclasses, breaking the hierarchy and the Open/Closed Principle.

smells.name: Inappropriate Static
smells.summary: Static functions that should be polymorphic or that hide dependencies, making them hard to replace and test.

name: Change Preventers
description: Changing something in one place forces many changes in other places.

smells.name: Divergent Change
smells.summary: A single class is changed for many different reasons (violates the Single Responsibility Principle).

smells.name: Shotgun Surgery
smells.summary: A single conceptual change requires many small edits across many different classes.

smells.name: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies
smells.summary: Every time you add a subclass to one hierarchy you must add one to a parallel hierarchy.

smells.name: Combinatorial Explosion
smells.summary: Many pieces of code do the same thing with different combinations of data or behavior.

name: Dispensables
description: Something pointless or unneeded whose absence would make the code cleaner and easier to understand.

smells.name: Duplicate Code
smells.summary: The same logic appears in several places; every change must be replicated and it is easy to miss one.

smells.name: Lazy Class / Lazy Element
smells.summary: A class or function that does so little it does not justify its existence.

smells.name: Data Class
smells.summary: Classes with only fields and getters/setters while the logic that manipulates them lives elsewhere.

smells.name: Dead Code
smells.summary: Variables, parameters, functions or branches that are never used or executed.

smells.name: Speculative Generality
smells.summary: Abstractions, hooks and parameters created "just in case" that nobody needs (YAGNI).

smells.name: Comments (as Deodorant)
smells.summary: Comments used to explain confusing code instead of rewriting it so it explains itself.

smells.name: Clutter
smells.summary: Empty constructors, unused variables, unnecessary imports and noise that adds nothing.

name: Couplers
description: Excessive coupling between classes, or excessive delegation.

smells.name: Feature Envy
smells.summary: A method uses another class's data more than its own.

smells.name: Inappropriate Intimacy
smells.summary: A class reaches into the internal details (private fields, state) of another class.

smells.name: Message Chains (Train Wreck)
smells.sources: Fowler 1999; Clean Code G36; Law of Demeter
smells.summary: Chains like a.getB().getC().getD() couple the client to the whole navigation structure.

smells.name: Middle Man
smells.summary: A class where most methods simply delegate to another class.

smells.name: Incomplete Library Class
smells.summary: A library does not provide what you need and the extension logic ends up scattered across the code.

smells.name: Global Data
smells.summary: Global state that can be modified from anywhere, impossible to trace and to test.

smells.name: Insider Trading
smells.summary: Modules that secretly exchange internal data instead of using explicit interfaces.

smells.name: Artificial Coupling
smells.summary: Unrelated elements become coupled because they are declared together (generic constants inside concrete classes).

smells.name: Hidden Temporal Coupling
smells.summary: Calls must happen in a specific order but nothing in the code enforces it or makes it visible.

name: Data Dealers
description: Problems in how data is represented, mutated and shared.

smells.name: Mutable Data
smells.summary: Data that changes in unexpected places causing bugs that are hard to trace.

smells.name: Magic Numbers / Magic Strings
smells.summary: Unnamed literals whose meaning must be guessed.

smells.name: Boolean Blindness
smells.summary: Booleans lose the meaning of what they represent, making calls like f(true, false) unreadable.

smells.name: Null Check / Null Abuse
smells.summary: Returning and checking null everywhere instead of using null objects, optionals or explicit errors.

smells.name: Status Variable
smells.summary: Mutable flag variables used to control the flow of loops or functions.

smells.name: Loops / Imperative Loops
smells.summary: Hand-written loops where a collection pipeline (map/filter/reduce) would express intent better.

name: Functions & Conditional Logic
description: Signatures, side effects and conditional logic that are hard to understand or use.

smells.name: Output Arguments
smells.summary: Parameters the function mutates to return results instead of using the return value.

smells.name: Flag / Selector Arguments
smells.summary: A boolean or enum makes the function do different things: it is really several functions.

smells.name: Side Effects
smells.summary: A function promises one thing but also silently changes global state, its arguments or the system.

smells.name: Deep Nesting / Arrow Code
smells.summary: Many levels of nested if/for form an arrow shape and hide the main path.

smells.name: Complicated Boolean Expression
smells.summary: Long, opaque conditions that should be encapsulated in well-named functions or variables.

smells.name: Negative Conditionals
smells.summary: Conditions expressed negatively (or double-negatively) are harder to read than their positive form.

smells.name: Mixed Levels of Abstraction
smells.summary: A function mixes low-level details with high-level operations.

smells.name: Command-Query Separation Violation
smells.summary: Functions that both change state and return information, creating ambiguity.

name: Error Handling
description: Errors that are ignored, hidden or used as a control-flow mechanism.

smells.name: Swallowed Exceptions / Afraid to Fail
smells.summary: Catching errors and doing nothing (or only logging), leaving the system in an inconsistent state.

smells.name: Returning Error Codes
smells.summary: Returning -1, null or magic codes instead of explicit errors that cannot be ignored.

smells.name: Exceptions for Control Flow
smells.summary: Using exceptions for expected cases of the normal flow instead of conditions.

smells.name: Overridden Safeties
smells.summary: Turning off compiler warnings, linters or failing tests to "keep going".

smells.name: Incorrect Behavior at the Boundaries
smells.summary: Boundary conditions (empty, zero, last element, off-by-one) scattered around or not handled.

name: Comments
description: Comments that add nothing, lie, or replace good code (Clean Code C1-C5).

smells.name: Inappropriate Information
smells.summary: Comments holding information that belongs in another system: author, dates, change history, tickets.

smells.name: Obsolete Comment
smells.summary: Comments that have drifted away from the code and now lie.

smells.name: Redundant Comment
smells.summary: Comments that repeat what the code already says clearly.

smells.name: Poorly Written Comment
smells.summary: Ambiguous, rambling or sloppy comments that confuse more than they help.

smells.name: Commented-Out Code
smells.summary: Blocks of commented-out code nobody dares to delete; that is what version control is for.

name: Names
description: Names that fail to communicate, confuse or lie (Clean Code N1-N7).

smells.name: Mysterious / Uncommunicative Name
smells.summary: Names like d, tmp, data2 or proc that do not reveal intent.

smells.name: Names at the Wrong Level of Abstraction
smells.summary: Names that reveal the implementation (dialModem) instead of the concept (connect).

smells.name: Non-Standard Nomenclature
smells.summary: Ignoring well-known pattern names and the conventions of the language and the domain.

smells.name: Ambiguous Name
smells.summary: Names open to several interpretations, such as doRename or process.

smells.name: Short Names for Long Scopes
smells.summary: Single-letter names used in wide scopes or long-lived variables.

smells.name: Encodings in Names / Type Embedded in Name
smells.summary: Hungarian notation, m_ prefixes or embedded types (strName, needless IUserInterface).

smells.name: Names Should Describe Side Effects
smells.summary: A getX() that also creates, saves or modifies things without its name saying so.

smells.name: Inconsistent Names
smells.summary: The same concept goes by several names (fetch/get/retrieve, user/client/customer).

smells.name: Binary Operator in Name
smells.summary: Names containing And/Or (validateAndSave) reveal that the function does more than one thing.

smells.name: Fallacious Method Name
smells.summary: The name promises something different from what the method does (isValid that mutates, getX that returns something else).

name: General
description: General design and readability heuristics (Clean Code G1-G36).

smells.name: Multiple Languages in One Source File
smells.summary: SQL, HTML, JS, XML... mixed in the same source file.

smells.name: Obvious Behavior Is Unimplemented
smells.sources: Clean Code G2 (Principle of Least Surprise)
smells.summary: A function does not do what anyone would expect from its name or type.

smells.name: Too Much Information / Indecent Exposure
smells.summary: Wide interfaces that expose internal details that should be private.

smells.name: Vertical Separation
smells.summary: Variables and functions defined far away from where they are used.

smells.name: Obscured Intent / Clever Code
smells.summary: Compact, cryptic code that shows off cleverness but hides what it does.

smells.name: Misplaced Responsibility
smells.summary: Code placed where it was convenient for the author, not where the reader would look for it.

smells.name: Missing Explanatory Variables
smells.summary: Complex expressions not broken down into well-named intermediate variables.

smells.name: Logical Dependency Not Made Physical
smells.summary: A module assumes something about another (a size, an order) without explicitly asking for it.

smells.name: Prefer Structure over Convention
smells.summary: Relying on conventions ("remember to add a case") instead of letting the structure enforce it.

smells.name: Be Precise / Imprecision
smells.summary: Using float for money, ignoring concurrency or assuming a query returns a single result.

smells.name: Configurable Data at Low Levels
smells.summary: Configuration constants buried deep in the code.

smells.name: Oddball Solution
smells.summary: The same problem is solved in different ways in different parts of the system.

smells.name: Complicated Regex Expression
smells.summary: Long, cryptic regular expressions without names, comments or decomposition.

smells.name: Callback Hell / Pyramid of Doom
smells.summary: Callbacks nested inside callbacks make asynchronous flow unreadable.

name: Test Smells
description: Smells in test code (Clean Code T1-T9 and xUnit Test Patterns).

smells.name: Insufficient Tests
smells.summary: Only the happy path is tested; there is no coverage tool and relevant cases go untested.

smells.name: Ignored Tests
smells.summary: Disabled or skipped tests with no documented reason that nobody ever re-enables.

smells.name: Untested Boundary Conditions
smells.summary: Boundary cases and the neighborhood of known bugs are not tested.

smells.name: Slow Tests
smells.summary: Tests that depend on network, disk or real waits and are so slow nobody runs them.

smells.name: Assertion Roulette
smells.summary: Many assertions without messages in one test: when it fails you cannot tell which one or why.

smells.name: Mystery Guest
smells.summary: The test depends on external resources (files, DB) that are invisible when reading it.

smells.name: Eager Test
smells.summary: A single test verifies many different behaviors at once.

smells.name: Conditional Test Logic
smells.summary: Tests with if, loops or try/catch that may never execute their assertions.

smells.name: Sleepy Test
smells.summary: Using sleep to wait for asynchrony: slow, non-deterministic tests.

smells.name: Fragile Test / Testing Implementation Details
smells.summary: Tests coupled to implementation details that break with any refactoring.

smells.name: Interdependent Tests / Shared Fixture
smells.summary: Tests sharing mutable state that only pass in a specific order.

name: Environment
description: Development environment problems: build and tests (Clean Code E1-E2).

smells.name: Build Requires More Than One Step
smells.summary: Building the project requires a manual sequence of commands, files and tribal knowledge.

smells.name: Tests Require More Than One Step
smells.summary: Running all the tests cannot be done with a single command.

smells.name: Mutable Default Argument
smells.summary: Default values are evaluated once: a default list is shared between calls.

smells.name: Bare except
smells.summary: `except:` catches even KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit and hides real errors.

smells.name: Wildcard Import
smells.summary: `from x import *` pollutes the namespace and hides where each name comes from.

smells.name: Using `is` for Value Comparison
smells.summary: Comparing values with `is` works by accident (integer caching) and fails intermittently.

smells.name: Late-Binding Closures
smells.summary: Lambdas created in a loop capture the variable, not its value: they all see the last one.

smells.name: Java-style Getters and Setters
smells.summary: Trivial get_x/set_x methods instead of attributes or @property.

smells.name: Not Using Context Managers
smells.summary: Opening resources without `with`, risking leaks when an exception is raised.

smells.name: range(len()) Iteration
smells.summary: Manual indexing instead of iterating directly or using enumerate/zip.

smells.name: Type Checking with type()
smells.summary: `type(x) == Class` breaks inheritance; use isinstance or, better, polymorphism/duck typing.

smells.name: String Concatenation in a Loop
smells.summary: `s += x` in a loop is quadratic and hard to read; use str.join or f-strings.

smells.name: global Statement
smells.summary: Functions that modify module-level variables through `global`.

smells.name: Monkey Patching in Production Code
smells.summary: Modifying third-party classes or modules at runtime from production code.

smells.name: Stringly-typed Dicts instead of Classes
smells.summary: Passing dicts with magic keys instead of dataclasses, NamedTuple or TypedDict.

smells.name: Reinventing the Standard Library
smells.summary: Re-implementing by hand what collections, itertools, pathlib, etc. already provide.

smells.name: Shadowing Built-ins
smells.summary: Naming variables list, dict, id, type, input... hiding the built-in functions.

smells.name: assert for Data Validation
smells.summary: asserts disappear under `python -O`; they cannot be used to validate input data.

smells.name: Inconsistent Return Statements
smells.summary: Some branches return a value while others implicitly return None.

smells.name: Overly Complex Comprehension
smells.summary: Comprehensions with several for/if clauses and nested logic on one line.

smells.name: Import-time Side Effects
smells.summary: Connections, file reads or heavy work executed when a module is imported.

smells.name: Missing Type Hints / Any Abuse
smells.summary: Public APIs without annotations or full of Any, defeating static analysis.

smells.name: async void Methods
smells.summary: Exceptions that cannot be caught and crash the process, and calls that cannot be awaited.

smells.name: Sync over Async (.Result / .Wait())
smells.summary: Blocking on Tasks causes deadlocks and thread-pool starvation.

smells.name: Missing using / IDisposable Leak
smells.summary: IDisposable resources that are never released (connections, streams, sockets).

smells.name: Rethrowing with `throw ex`
smells.summary: `throw ex;` resets the stack trace and loses where the error happened.

smells.name: Catching General Exception
smells.summary: Indiscriminate `catch (Exception)` that hides programming errors.

smells.name: String Concatenation in Loops
smells.summary: `+=` on strings in loops allocates thousands of objects; use StringBuilder or string.Join.

smells.name: Multiple Enumeration of IEnumerable
smells.summary: Iterating a deferred IEnumerable several times repeats queries or side effects.

smells.name: new HttpClient per Request
smells.summary: Creating and disposing HttpClient on every call exhausts sockets; use IHttpClientFactory.

smells.name: DateTime.Now Hidden Dependency
smells.summary: Logic that depends on the system clock and cannot be tested deterministically.

smells.name: Service Locator Anti-pattern
smells.summary: Asking a global container for dependencies hides the real dependencies of a class.

smells.name: Static Mutable State
smells.summary: Mutable static fields shared across threads and requests.

smells.name: Anemic Domain Model
smells.summary: Entities without behavior manipulated by services that hold all the logic.

smells.name: Locking on this / Public Objects
smells.summary: Locking on publicly reachable objects lets external code cause deadlocks.

smells.name: Exposing Mutable Collections
smells.summary: Public List<T> properties with setters that let callers break invariants.

smells.name: Null-Forgiving Operator Abuse
smells.summary: Silencing nullability warnings with `!` instead of handling null.

smells.name: Side Effects in LINQ
smells.summary: Mutating state inside Select/Where; deferred execution makes it unpredictable.

smells.name: Fake Async (Task.Run Wrapping)
smells.summary: Wrapping synchronous code in Task.Run inside a library to look asynchronous.

smells.name: Control Freak (Newing Dependencies)
smells.summary: Instantiating dependencies inside the class prevents injecting and testing them.

smells.name: #region Abuse
smells.summary: Using #region to hide huge classes instead of splitting them.

smells.name: Magic Configuration Strings
smells.summary: Reading configuration with scattered string keys instead of strongly typed IOptions<T>.

smells.name: Prop Drilling
smells.summary: Passing props through many intermediate components that do not use them.

smells.name: God Component / Large Component
smells.summary: A component that fetches data, manages state, holds business logic and renders the whole UI.

smells.name: Derived State via useEffect
smells.sources: react.dev: You Might Not Need an Effect
smells.summary: Computing in an effect + setState something that can be calculated during render.

smells.name: Props Copied into State
smells.summary: Initializing useState from a prop creates two sources of truth that drift apart.

smells.name: Missing Effect Cleanup
smells.summary: Subscriptions, timers or listeners that are never removed.

smells.name: Stale Closure / Missing Dependencies
smells.summary: Omitting hook dependencies makes them read stale values.

smells.name: Direct State Mutation
smells.summary: Mutating state objects or arrays instead of creating new ones: React does not re-render.

smells.name: Array Index as Key
smells.summary: Using the index as key in lists that change mixes up state and DOM.

smells.name: any Abuse
smells.summary: `any` switches off the type system and silently propagates errors.

smells.name: Non-null Assertion Abuse
smells.summary: `value!` lies to the compiler about values that may be null.

smells.name: Type Assertion (as) Abuse
smells.summary: `as Type` to force external data without validating it at runtime.

smells.name: Component Defined Inside Component
smells.summary: Defining components in another component's body recreates them on every render and loses their state.

smells.name: Boolean Props Explosion
smells.summary: isPrimary, isDanger, isSmall... impossible combinations instead of a typed variant.

smells.name: Nested Ternaries in JSX
smells.summary: Ternaries inside ternaries to decide what to render.

smells.name: Chains of Effects
smells.summary: Effects updating state that triggers other effects in cascade.

smells.name: Monolithic / Overused Context
smells.summary: A single giant context for everything causes massive re-renders and coupling.

smells.name: Premature Memoization
smells.summary: useMemo/useCallback/memo everywhere without measuring, adding complexity without benefit.

smells.name: Fetch in Effect without Abort
smells.summary: Requests in effects without cancellation: stale responses overwrite fresh ones.

smells.name: Stringly Typed Code
smells.summary: Free-form strings where a union of literals or a discriminated type would provide safety.

smells.name: Too Many Related useState
smells.summary: Many related useState calls that must change together; useReducer or an object is better.

smells.name: Business Logic in Components
smells.summary: Business rules mixed with JSX instead of living in hooks or pure modules.

smells.name: Indiscriminate Props Spreading
smells.summary: `{...props}` passing unknown attributes to the DOM and hiding the component contract.

smells.name: Ignored Errors
smells.summary: Discarding errors with `_` or not checking them at all.

smells.name: panic for Control Flow
smells.summary: Using panic/recover for expected errors instead of returning error.

smells.name: Interface Pollution
smells.summary: Interfaces created on the producer side "just in case" with a single implementation.

smells.name: Empty Interface Abuse
smells.summary: Using any where a concrete or generic type would provide type safety.

smells.name: Goroutine Leak
smells.summary: Goroutines blocked forever with no way to finish.

smells.name: Missing Context Propagation
smells.summary: Ignoring context.Context: no cancellation and no timeouts.

smells.name: Naked Returns in Long Functions
smells.summary: Bare returns in long functions with named results.

smells.name: init() Abuse
smells.summary: Logic with side effects, I/O or hidden errors inside init functions.

smells.name: Mutable Package-level State
smells.summary: Mutable package-level variables that prevent parallel tests.

smells.name: Stuttering Names
smells.summary: user.UserService, http.HTTPServer: repeating the package name.

smells.name: Getters with Get Prefix
smells.summary: In Go the getter for owner is Owner(), not GetOwner().

smells.name: Error Strings Style
smells.summary: Error messages capitalized, ending in punctuation or lacking context.

smells.name: Lost Error Wrapping (%v vs %w)
smells.summary: Formatting with %v or comparing with == prevents errors.Is/As.

smells.name: defer in Loop
smells.summary: defers run when the function returns, not per iteration: resources pile up.

smells.name: Loop Variable Capture
smells.summary: Before Go 1.22 every goroutine/closure shared the loop variable.

smells.name: Copying sync.Mutex
smells.summary: Value receivers copy the mutex and synchronization disappears.

smells.name: Typed nil in Interface
smells.summary: Returning a nil pointer as error yields a non-nil interface.

smells.name: utils / common Packages
smells.sources: Dave Cheney; Go blog: Package names
smells.summary: Catch-all packages with no cohesion or meaningful name.

smells.name: time.After in Loops
smells.summary: Each iteration creates a new timer; use time.NewTimer or context.

smells.name: WaitGroup.Add inside Goroutine
smells.summary: Calling Add inside the goroutine races with Wait.

smells.name: Concurrent Map Access without Sync
smells.summary: Reading and writing a map from several goroutines without protection.

smells.name: Pointer to Interface
smells.summary: *MyInterface is almost never needed and reveals confusion.
